answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: The final reply is split into "## Fix first: before launch" (items 1-4, each of which "can leave a skipper outside the harbour or with no booking") and "## Fix next" (items 5-11). Its closing paragraph names what it could not check: "I didn't test with real screen readers (VoiceOver or TalkBack) or at 200% browser zoom" and "it's worth running the main booking with a few real skippers once points 1-4 are fixed", plus "Please confirm" on whether a real backend exists.

mapping.title: Tide table in UTC while arrival time is local (BST); dropdown names no time zone
mapping.reason: Same problem as D05: high-water times are given in UTC, the arrival-time list is local time, and on 17 October (BST) a skipper planning from the table is an hour out for the sill gate.

mapping.title: Arrival-time picker shows no gate window and accepts times when the gate is shut
mapping.reason: D09 exactly: the hour list accepts a closed-gate time (the review booked 06:00 on 17 October) with no warning, and the gate rule sits only under the tide table instead of next to the time choice.

mapping.title: Gate window not repeated on the berth list, review or confirmation page
mapping.reason: Broader statement of D11's first omission: the confirmation never shows the sill-gate window for the booked day. The review's fix (repeat the window on the review and confirmation pages) would fix that part of D11.

mapping.title: Tide table covers only 17-23 October while the date picker runs to March 2027
mapping.reason: Not among the seeded defects. A skipper booking any date outside that week has no high-water or gate information for their day and cannot plan arrival over the sill, which is the safety-relevant decision this flow exists to support.

mapping.title: "Booking stopped" (BK-409) dead end: no reason, next step or link; berth chosen before the length is known
mapping.reason: D04 exactly: an over-length boat replaces the form with Booking stopped and a bare reference, with no explanation, nothing kept, and no way to correct the length or pick a longer berth. The 'picks a berth blind' remark is the same problem's cause, offered as a fix.

mapping.title: "Length" field ambiguous (hull vs overall), no unit; berth cards do not say LOA
mapping.reason: D03 exactly: the field is labelled only Length, so a skipper may enter hull length (9.6 m) and pass the check for a berth the 10.4 m LOA boat does not fit.

mapping.title: Boat form cleared on Back (pageshow reset in app.js)
mapping.reason: D07 exactly: going back from review empties every boat field because the page resets the form on pageshow, so one correction means retyping all of it.

mapping.title: Confirm booking sends nothing to a backend; name and mobile discarded
mapping.reason: The review itself says it assumed a front-end prototype and asks the owner to confirm. A static prototype having no backend is not a usability problem for skippers using this flow, and the harm described is conditional on a live build the review has not seen.

mapping.title: Booking reference (date + berth code) not unique
mapping.reason: Speculative implementation detail: two bookings of the same berth on the same day would be a double booking the system should not allow anyway, and the reference format does not hinder a skipper using the flow.

mapping.title: "Change dates" hidden behind an unlabelled three-dot button on the berth list
mapping.reason: D01 exactly: the only route back to the dates is inside an unlabelled three-dot menu, so a skipper whose arrival day changes sees nothing to tap.

mapping.title: Review page has no Change links on any row
mapping.reason: Not a seeded defect (D02 is about a step indicator, which Change links on the review page would not supply). A skipper who spots a mistake on the review page can only use the browser Back button, which in turn wipes the boat form, so errors go through or the booking is abandoned.

mapping.title: Review page omits the draught
mapping.reason: Not seeded. The review page is where a skipper checks what they entered before confirming; a draught that is collected but never shown cannot be checked, so a mistyped value reaches the office unseen, and draught matters for a drying wall berth and the sill.

mapping.title: Confirmation omits arrival time, gate window, boat name, total, pay-on-arrival note and what happens next
mapping.reason: Broader statement of D11: the confirmation gives a reference but no arrival instructions. The review asks for the gate window and for "what happens next (for example: call or radio the office on approach)", which are D11's missing gate window and VHF call.

mapping.title: MMSI required with no hint what it is; many small boats have none
mapping.reason: D10 exactly: MMSI is mandatory with no explanation of the abbreviation or what to do if the boat has none; the review's fix (make it optional and add a one-line hint) fixes it.

mapping.title: Terminology changes: visitor berth, pontoon space, mooring booking
mapping.reason: D08 exactly: one thing has three names across the flow; the review names the same three terms and asks for "berth" throughout.

mapping.title: Error messages give no format help ("Enter the length", "Enter the MMSI")
mapping.reason: D10's description includes that the error message only repeats Enter the MMSI; the review's fix ("The MMSI is 9 digits") addresses that facet. The length half overlaps D03's missing unit, but the item is one problem about format-less errors and D10 is the defect that names the error message.

mapping.title: Draught collected but never checked against the sill or berth depth
mapping.reason: Not seeded. The site asks for draught, notes that wall berth 2 dries out and that the sill has a depth limit, yet lets a deep-draught boat book either with no warning, so a skipper can arrive at a berth or gate they cannot use.
